concerns.text: The plan validates the HMM‑derived regimes using a ‘10‑day rolling absolute‑return’ proxy, which is a deterministic transformation of the same log‑return series that serves as the HMM emission feature (squared returns). Because the validation metric is derived from the same underlying data, it is not truly independent; the test risks circularity—regimes are judged distinct on a statistic that is functionally linked to the predictor used to define them. A scientifically sound validation should employ a volatility estimator that uses information not employed in the HMM fitting (e.g., the Garman‑Klass estimator based on OHLCV data as required by FR‑010). As currently specified, the regime‑distinctness test may always confirm differences by construction, undermining the empirical claim.
